Subject: Request: chunked ledger delta exports + assertion format for SOC 2 evidence

Hi Nikhil / Kimberly,

We're preparing the SOC 2 evidence package for our annual audit and need a concrete export that shows admin/operator actions and session traces for a given tenant over a window. Auditor asked for a "delta-style" export so they can validate continuity between snapshots rather than a full bulk dump.

Specifically we need:
- A recommended chunking/chunk-size approach for large windows (e.g., >30M events) so we can ingest incrementally
- A canonical manifest with signed assertions (proof the bundle is complete and unmodified)
- Checksums and recommended transport options (S3 presigned vs SFTP vs managed transfer)
- Retention/TTL guidance for exported bundles (auditors typically want 90 days hot, 12 months accessible)

Can Redwood provide a suggested format and a sample bundle we can test with our ingestion team? Also please call out which event types are guaranteed in the ledger (authn, authz changes, API keys, admin console actions, session start/stop, and operator-triggered model rollbacks).

Thanks — we'd like to close this by EOW so we can hand to the auditor.

Best,
Rebecca

Subject: Re: Request: chunked ledger delta exports + assertion format for SOC 2 evidence

Rebecca — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Kim/Logan and Marissa from ops so we can give a runnable delivery option.

Summary of what Redwood can provide (short):
- Event coverage: our admin ledger includes: account-level authn events (login success/fail), authz changes (role grants/revokes), API key lifecycle (create, rotate, revoke), console actions (user/role changes, model deploy/rollback), operator session start/stop and operator-executed API calls. We also include system-generated autoscale/health actions as separate event types.

- Chunking: we produce delta bundles as chronological slabs (time-range based slices). Default slab size is configurable by token count or event-count; practical default we use for large customers is ~6-hour slabs (approx 10M events) but we can support custom thresholds (by MB, event count). Each slab is a gzipped newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) file where each row is an event with a monotonic sequence_id.

- Manifest + assertions: each slab is accompanied by a manifest.json that contains: slab_id, start_time, end_time, event_count, first_seq, last_seq, and checksum (SHA256) of the slab file. We can produce either a PKCS#7 signature (Redwood signs with our key) or provide an HMAC-SHA256 assertion keyed by a customer-provided shared secret. For auditor workflows we recommend PKCS#7 signed manifests plus a chain-of-custody file (attestation.json) that contains a Redwood-signed assertion about completeness and ordering.

- Transport: supported options — presigned S3 URLs (preferred for scale), SFTP (endpoint per customer), or push to your S3 via cross-account role. Presigned S3 + signed manifest is the most commonly accepted pattern. All transports include an MD5/SHA checksum in the transfer metadata.

- Retention & TTL on exports: we can retain exported bundles in our staging for 14 days by default; longer staging is available (30/90/365 days) under a retention SLA. The exported objects themselves can be pushed to your tenant bucket and retained per your lifecycle rules (we recommend 90 days hot, 365 days archive).

I'll attach a short spec and a tiny sample bundle for ingestion testing. Can you confirm which assertion type the audit team prefers (Redwood PKCS#7 signature vs HMAC keyed by Novomed)? Also confirm target slab size (time-window or event count) and whether you want per-tenant packaging or combined multi-tenant export (we default to per-tenant for audit traceability).

Next steps:
- If you want PKCS#7 we will deliver keys and attestation; if HMAC please share the HMAC key provisioning contact or a secure sftp/secret-vault method.
- We can schedule a 30-min handoff with your ingestion team tomorrow.

Regards,

Rebecca / team — a few implementation notes from the operations/compliance side, plus a small sample manifest attached for Novomed ingestion engineers. Quoting Nikhil below where helpful.

Operational recommendations (to avoid auditor pushback):
- Manifest canonicalization: use deterministic JSON (sorted keys, UTF-8, no whitespace) before signing to ensure signature reproducibility. Include manifest version and Redwood runtime build_id.
- Checksums: slab SHA256 + manifest SHA256. Additionally include a per-event lightweight hash (first 8 hex chars of SHA256) as an index column; this lets auditors sample without re-downloading full slabs.
- Sequence monotonicity: every event has a sequence_id+node_id. Completeness assertion should reference first_seq/last_seq and a signed sequence range. Avoid relying only on timestamps because clock skew can exist.
- Chain-of-custody: attestation.json should include a transfer_receipt array with: transport_method, presigned_url_ttl, transfer_time_rfc3339, transfer_checksum, and optional storage_location (s3://novomed-audit/2026/06/07/).
- Retention: for SOC 2 our compliance team recommends 90d immediate accessibility + immutable backup for 365d. If Novomed requires longer, we can negotiate extended staging retention under the Dedicated contract.

Small caveat: for edge events (automatic model-rollback triggered by safety filter), we currently include the triggering operator id if the rollback was manual; fully automated system actions will be flagged as system_actor. If the auditor needs per-machine end-to-end debugging traces we can include the runbook id but that contains internal infra identifiers (we can redact if needed).

Attached: sample manifest (manifest-sample.json) and a 3-slab index. Logan/Marissa — flag if any operational limits (eg max slab size by CPU for on-demand exports).

Kimberly Park

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with what our auditor needs. Couple quick confirmations: 

- We'll accept Redwood PKCS#7-signed manifests (auditor prefers a third-party signature so they can validate issuer).
- Delivery: presigned S3 per-slab with TTL 48h is fine; include transfer_receipt in attestation.json.
- Slab size: let's start with 4-hour slabs for the initial sample (Novomed ingestion team prefers smaller windows to parallelize).
- Retention: Novomed will copy exported objects to our bucket and keep 90d hot + 12mo cold.

Please go ahead and produce:
1) A sample set for tenant novomed (3 slabs, 4h each) pushed via presigned S3 (we'll use the sample URLs to test)
2) A PKCS#7-signed attestation.json referencing the slabs and containing checksums

I'll route POQ to our cloud team for the HMAC key if we later choose HMAC; for now PKCS#7 is preferred. Can we schedule the 30-min ingestion handoff Friday 06/11? 10:00-10:30 PT works for us.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
